# 2025 Somerset–London tornado

The “2025 Somerset–London tornado” is not documented by reliable sources as an actual event. As of 11 December 2025, there are no official or reputable media reports of a tornado with a continuous track from Somerset to London, nor do authoritative catalogues or archives use the name “2025 Somerset–London tornado.” The United Kingdom’s principal meteorological and research organisations, along with major national and local news outlets and official emergency services communications, contain no record of a tornado that traversed the distance between Somerset and London in 2025, and the term does not appear in their reporting or incident logs . In the UK, verified tornado reports are typically catalogued by the Tornado and Storm Research Organisation (TORRO) and in the European Severe Weather Database (ESWD); neither platform lists an event under this name, and no Met Office press communications adopt this nomenclature for any 2025 incident .

## Existence and nomenclature

- Naming and recognition: The designation “2025 Somerset–London tornado” is not employed by the UK Met Office, TORRO, ESWD, or major news outlets. These bodies are the usual sources for verified naming and documentation of significant UK tornadoes. As of 11 December 2025, neither TORRO’s publicly available materials nor the Met Office’s press archive include any report or analysis of a tornado identified as connecting Somerset and London in 2025 . 
- Media and official communications: Major national media typically cover urban tornadoes (particularly in London) and unusual UK tornadoes; however, BBC News and other leading outlets do not carry contemporaneous reports of a long-track Somerset-to-London tornado in 2025 . Likewise, incident postings by London Fire Brigade and local government communications in Somerset contain no relevant entries adopting this name or describing an event of comparable scale and trajectory .
- Classification: In the absence of recognisable sources adopting the term, and without a documented track and damage survey, there is no basis to classify a “Somerset–London” 2025 tornado as a single long-track tornado or an outbreak. UK tornado events, when they occur, are generally analysed and assigned intensities by TORRO on the T-scale and sometimes correlated with other data in ESWD .

## Meteorological background and UK tornado climatology

- Tornadoes in the UK: Tornadoes do occur in the UK, though usually of limited path length and intensity compared with the strongest US events. They are often associated with convective storms embedded in frontal systems or localised supercell structures under favourable wind shear, with typical tracks measured in kilometres rather than hundreds of kilometres .
- Rarity of long-track tornadoes: A continuous path extending from Somerset to London would imply an unusually long and sustained tornadic vortex for UK conditions. Such events would attract immediate attention from the Met Office, TORRO, and national media due to their rarity and potential for significant damage. No such attention or documentation appears in these sources for 2025 .

## Reported chronology and path

- Dates and times: There are no verified dates, times, or radar-confirmed tracks associated with a “Somerset–London tornado” in 2025 in authoritative records .
- Geographic scope and continuity: UK tornado documentation normally specifies start and end points, path length and width, and affected communities. No official chronology, geospatial path, or continuity evidence is available for a tornado traversing Somerset and reaching any London boroughs in 2025 .

## Intensity and rating

- TORRO and EF ratings: In the UK, TORRO typically assesses tornado intensity using the T-scale. Occasionally, comparisons to the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale are discussed in research or media. For 2025, there is no TORRO rating or official intensity assessment for a Somerset–London tornado because no such event is documented by relevant organisations .
- Wind speeds: In the absence of a documented event and damage survey, no maximum wind speed estimates exist under this name.

## Impacts

- Human impacts: No fatalities, injuries, or displacements attributable to a “Somerset–London tornado” in 2025 are reported by national media or official bodies .
- Property and infrastructure: There are no verified reports of damage to homes, businesses, schools, hospitals, or critical infrastructure linked to such an event, nor are there records of widespread utility outages or transport disruptions specifically attributed to a tornado crossing from Somerset to London in 2025 .
- Economic losses: No insured or total loss estimates exist for an event under this name.

## Emergency response and aftermath

- Emergency services: Neither the London Fire Brigade’s incidents feed nor Somerset Council’s news updates contain records of tornado-related emergency responses consistent with a single event spanning Somerset to London in 2025 .
- Recovery and policy discussions: There is no evidence of recovery operations, official inquiries, or policy debates prompted by a 2025 “Somerset–London tornado” in UK governmental or research outputs .

## Assessments and controversies

- Verification practices: UK tornado verification typically relies on ground surveys, radar-based storm-scale analysis, photographic and video documentation, and structured collection of witness reports—procedures run or collated by organisations such as TORRO and compiled in databases like ESWD . 
- Absence of records: The lack of entries in these sources, together with the absence of contemporaneous national media coverage or official communications, indicates that the “2025 Somerset–London tornado” is not a recognised meteorological event as of 11 December 2025 .

## Historical context and significance

- Context: The UK experiences several tornadoes each year, most of them weak and short-lived by global standards. Notable UK tornadoes that impact urban areas or that are comparatively strong typically receive immediate and sustained coverage by national outlets and are documented by TORRO and the Met Office .
- Significance of the claimed path: A verified tornado maintaining a continuous track from Somerset to London would be exceptional in UK records. The absence of such documentation in 2025 from both meteorological authorities and media suggests the term “2025 Somerset–London tornado” lacks basis in published, reliable evidence .

## Media coverage and documentation

- National outlets: BBC News and other major UK newsrooms publish timely, prominent reports when tornadoes affect populated areas. No such coverage exists for a 2025 tornado crossing Somerset and London, and the term is not used by these outlets .
- Official channels: Met Office press pages, London Fire Brigade incident postings, and Somerset Council news updates do not contain entries that correspond to a cross-country tornado of this scale in 2025 .
- Research databases: TORRO’s public-facing materials and the ESWD do not list an event under this name or with an equivalent cross-regional trajectory for 2025 .

## Notes on related events

- Separate 2025 tornado reports: Any tornadoes that occurred in the UK in 2025 are catalogued on an event-by-event basis (e.g., by county, town, or specific localities) and are not aggregated under a “Somerset–London” label by the main UK meteorological and research bodies . Readers seeking verified 2025 incidents should consult the TORRO website and the ESWD for individual entries .

Sharing our weather and climate expertise - Met Office
===============

This website uses cookies
=========================

The Met Office website uses necessary cookies to make our site work. We also use optional cookies to help us improve your experience, understand how the site is being used for future improvements, and serve personalised advertising.

You can review the third-party vendors and how this information is being used below. You can also customise your consent preferences for cookies and identifying technologies.

**215** TCF vendors are seeking consent or wishing to pursue data processing purposes on the basis of their legitimate interests.

Personalised advertising adheres to the [IAB Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF).(Opens in a new window)](https://iabeurope.eu/iab-europe-transparency-consent-framework-policies/)

To agree to the use of these technologies select ‘Accept All’. You can change your preferences at any time by visiting our [cookie policy.(Opens in a new window)](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/legal/cookies)

How data is used Third party vendors

* * *

Purposes
--------

* * *

### Store and/or access information on a device

Cookies, device or similar online identifiers (e.g. login-based identifiers, randomly assigned identifiers, network based identifiers) together with other information (e.g. browser type and information, language, screen size, supported technologies etc.) can be stored or read on your device to recognise it each time it connects to an app or to a website, for one or several of the purposes presented here.

### Use limited data to select advertising

Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times an ad is presented to you).

- [x] purpose 1 On Off

### Create profiles for personalised advertising

Information about your activity on this service (such as forms you submit, content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (for example, information from your previous activity on this service and other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (that might include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present advertising that appears more relevant based on your possible interests by this and other entities.

Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on your advertising profiles, which can reflect your activity on this service or other websites or apps (like the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects.

- [x] purpose 3 On Off 

Read illustrations of possible use scenarios

* * *

### Create profiles to personalise content

Information about your activity on this service (for instance, forms you submit, non-advertising content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (such as your previous activity on this service or other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (which might for example include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present content that appears more relevant based on your possible interests, such as by adapting the order in which content is shown to you, so that it is even easier for you to find content that matches your interests.

- [x] purpose 4 On Off

* * *

### Use profiles to select personalised content

Content presented to you on this service can be based on your content personalisation profiles, which can reflect your activity on this or other services (for instance, the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects. This can for example be used to adapt the order in which content is shown to you, so that it is even easier for you to find (non-advertising) content that matches your interests.

- [x] purpose 5 On Off

* * *

### Measure advertising performance

Information regarding which advertising is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine how well an advert has worked for you or other users and whether the goals of the advertising were reached. For instance, whether you saw an ad, whether you clicked on it, whether it led you to buy a product or visit a website, etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of advertising campaigns.

* * *

### Measure content performance

Information regarding which content is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine whether the (non-advertising) content e.g. reached its intended audience and matched your interests. For instance, whether you read an article, watch a video, listen to a podcast or look at a product description, how long you spent on this service and the web pages you visit etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of (non-advertising) content that is shown to you.

Special Purposes
----------------

### Ensure security, prevent and detect fraud, and fix errors

Your data can be used to monitor for and prevent unusual and possibly fraudulent activity (for example, regarding advertising, ad clicks by bots), and ensure systems and processes work properly and securely. It can also be used to correct any problems you, the publisher or the advertiser may encounter in the delivery of content and ads and in your interaction with them.

Read illustrations of possible use scenarios

* * *

### Deliver and present advertising and content

Certain information (like an IP address or device capabilities) is used to ensure the technical compatibility of the content or advertising, and to facilitate the transmission of the content or ad to your device.

Read illustrations of possible use scenarios

* * *

### Save and communicate privacy choices

The choices you make regarding the purposes and entities listed in this notice are saved and made available to those entities in the form of digital signals (such as a string of characters). This is necessary in order to enable both this service and those entities to respect such choices.

Read illustrations of possible use scenarios

* * *

Features
--------

* * *

### Match and combine data from other data sources

Information about your activity on this service may be matched and combined with other information relating to you and originating from various sources (for instance your activity on a separate online service, your use of a loyalty card in-store, or your answers to a survey), in support of the purposes explained in this notice.

Read illustrations of possible use scenarios

* * *

### Link different devices

In support of the purposes explained in this notice, your device might be considered as likely linked to other devices that belong to you or your household (for instance because you are logged in to the same service on both your phone and your computer, or because you may use the same Internet connection on both devices).

Read illustrations of possible use scenarios

* * *

### Identify devices based on information transmitted automatically

Your device might be distinguished from other devices based on information it automatically sends when accessing the Internet (for instance, the IP address of your Internet connection or the type of browser you are using) in support of the purposes exposed in this notice.

Sharing our weather and climate expertise
=========================================

* * *

We are a world authority on weather and climate science.

Weather and climate stories are rarely out of the headlines, meaning that the views of our media-trained experts are frequently sought by media and others around the world.

Covering so many topics affecting the world’s weather and climate means we have a lot to talk about.

How you can follow us
---------------------

To keep yourself up to date you can find our conversations on many platforms and channels.

For the most up to date news on weather and climate you can [subscribe](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre/subscribe-to-email-alerts) to our press [releases](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre/weather-and-climate-news/index) and our [Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/@metoffice) channel.

For a more in-depth journey discovering more about the context of a range of weather and climate topics you can subscribe to our [blogposts](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/blog), or our [Climate](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre/climate-newsletter) and [Government & Industry](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre/government-and-industry-newsletter) newsletters.

If you are on the go and want instantly accessible up-to-the minute information you can engage with us on your favourite social media channels.

Media content and digital assets
--------------------------------

Visit our [media centre](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre) to access content and digital assets. Daily we produce a range of content, including presented forecasts, graphics, text and animations. Organisations can [register](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre/weather-and-climate-syndication-service) for this content, which can be inserted straight into news packages or used on websites.

Contact the press office
------------------------

Journalists wanting to start a conversation with us can [contact our team](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/contact-the-press-office) of press officers.
